نَقِدٌ , (L,) or ↓ نِقْدٌ , (K,) Slow in growing up into manhood, and having little flesh: (L, K:) [and so ↓ نُقْدٌ , accord. to the CK: but ويُضمّ is there put by mistake for وبِضَمٍّ: and the former, (S, L,) or ↓ نَقَدٌ , (K,) a boy despised and little in the eyes of others, that scarcely grows up into manhood; (S, L, K;) sometimes thus applied. (S, L.) ―
-b2- نَقِدٌ A horn eaten, or eroded, at the root. (L.) See also نَقِدَ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
